title: Fix Firestore security rules to allow authenticated users to create their own profile document

requirements.text: Update Firestore security rules to allow a newly authenticated user to CREATE their own profile document during signup by permitting writes when `request.auth != null` and `request.auth.uid == userId` for the profile document path used by the app (`users/{userId}`). Do not change any signup flow logic, admin/helper logic, or add new features.

quotes:
ONLY fix required:
Allow authenticated users to CREATE their own profile document
(using request.auth != null and request.auth.uid == userId)

acceptanceCriteria: In `frontend/firestore.rules`, the `match /users/{userId}` block includes an `allow create:` rule that evaluates to true only when the request is authenticated and `request.auth.uid == userId`.
After deploying the updated Firestore rules, a brand-new user completing signup can successfully write the profile document to `users/{auth.uid}` (no 'Missing or insufficient permissions' error).

Existing constraints remain unchanged: users cannot write other users' profile documents; admin/super_admin/helper_admin permissions and all other collection rules are not altered except as required to enable profile CREATE for self.

constraints: Do NOT create a new app or new project.
Do NOT clone, refactor, or restructure the codebase.
Do NOT touch signup flow logic (frontend signup implementation must remain unchanged).
Only modify Firestore security rules as needed to permit authenticated users to create their own profile document when `request.auth.uid == userId`.
After implementing the permissions fix, do not make additional changes in this area.
nonGoals: Any UI/UX changes to signup, login, or profile screens.
Any changes to approval flow, roles, admin dashboards, or helper admin capabilities.
Any changes to Firestore document schema or field names.
